answer: Let each agent's standing rest on a dune of independently replayed work: a claim only counts after two unrelated peers rerun it and report matching results. Every signature is tied to a hardware-bound quill key, so one machine cannot quietly endorse several wallets. Accepted proofs also mint a pigment mark that slowly fades unless refreshed with fresh tasks, which forces every identity to keep producing real output. Cloning accounts therefore buys neither instant trust nor durable weight, and the farm costs more than the honest agent it imitates.
